title: AI Just Helped Find Two New Superconductors
hook: Machine learning helped physicists find two new superconductors and sketch a faster route toward physics' biggest prize in the field: a superconductor that works at room temperature.
key_points: Researchers paired ML pre-screening with targeted quantum calculations to search far more candidate materials than manual theory allows.
The method flagged two new superconductors, YRu₂B₂ and LuRu₂B₂, whose superconductivity comes from electrons forming flat bands in a kagome lattice.
Of the 7,000+ superconductors known today, only about 20 were predicted by theory before being found — ML aims to flip that ratio.
The Aalto-led SuperC consortium's stated goal is a room-temperature superconductor by 2033.
content_html: Superconductors carry electric current with zero resistance, but almost every one we know was found by trial and error, not prediction — a compound gets made for some other reason, and only later does someone discover it superconducts. A team led by Päivi Törmä at Aalto University, working with Emilia Morosan's group at Rice University, wants to flip that process around.
extra_html: Their approach uses machine learning to rapidly pre-screen enormous numbers of elemental combinations, then hands the most promising candidates to detailed quantum calculations — work that used to take theorists years per compound. The method turned up two new superconductors, YRu₂B₂ and LuRu₂B₂, which owe their superconductivity to electrons forming "flat bands" in a kagome lattice, a geometric pattern named for a Japanese basket-weaving design. Of the more than 7,000 superconductors known today, only about 20 were predicted by theory before being found in the lab — the rest were serendipity. The team's SuperC consortium hopes ML screening at the scale of billions of candidate materials can flip that ratio, with a stated goal of identifying a room-temperature superconductor by 2033. Published in Physical Review Research.

flashcards.prompt: How did researchers speed up the search for new superconductors?
flashcards.back_html: They used machine learning to pre-screen huge numbers of candidate materials, then ran detailed quantum calculations only on the most promising few — skipping years of brute-force theory work per compound.

flashcards.prompt: What do the two new superconductors, YRu₂B₂ and LuRu₂B₂, have in common?

choices.text: Both get their superconductivity from electrons forming flat energy bands in a kagome lattice
Both already work at room temperature
Both were found with no theory involved, by pure trial and error

flashcards.explanation_html: Their shared trait is a kagome lattice — a geometric atomic arrangement — that produces flat electron bands conducive to superconductivity. Neither works at room temperature yet.

flashcards.prompt: Historically, how have most known superconductors been discovered?

choices.text: By serendipity — made in the lab first, only later found to superconduct
Almost all were predicted by theory before anyone made them
By scanning through every possible material with a supercomputer

flashcards.explanation_html: Of over 7,000 known superconductors, only about 20 were theoretically predicted first — the rest were found by accident. ML screening aims to reverse that ratio.
